देहरादून में रात का तापमान 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे।
शुक्रवार को पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ से बदलेगा मौसम।
जागरण संवाददाता, देहरादून। Uttarakhand Weather: उत्तराखंड में इन दिनों मौसम के अलग-अलग रंग देखने को मिल रहे हैं। दिनभर चटख धूप खिलने से अधिकतम तापमान सामान्य से ऊपर बना हुआ है, जबकि सुबह और शाम ठंड का अहसास बढ़ने लगा है। प्रदेश के ज्यादातर क्षेत्रों में न्यूनतम तापमान सामान्य से नीचे दर्ज किया जा रहा है। दिन और रात के तापमान में भी करीब दोगुना अंतर देखने को मिल रहा है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, अगले तीन दिन प्रदेश में मौसम का मिजाज लगभग इसी तरह बना रह सकता है। इसके बाद शुक्रवार को पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में मौसम करवट बदल सकता है।
उत्तराखंड में दिन में धूप, सुबह-शाम बढ़ी ठंड
प्रदेश के ज्यादातर हिस्सों में मौसम शुष्क बना हुआ है। दिन में तेज धूप के कारण गर्मी महसूस हो रही है, जबकि सूरज ढलने के बाद तापमान में गिरावट से ठंड बढ़ रही है। देहरादून में रात का तापमान 15 डिग्री सेल्सियस से नीचे पहुंच रहा है। दिन और रात के तापमान में अंतर बढ़ने से लोगों को सुबह-शाम गर्म कपड़ों की जरूरत महसूस होने लगी है।
शहर, अधिकतम, न्यूनतम
अगले तीन दिन मौसम शुष्क रहने के आसार, फिर लेगा करवट
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, मंगलवार को प्रदेशभर में मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है। अगले तीन दिन भी अधिकांश क्षेत्रों में बारिश के आसार कम हैं। हालांकि, आगामी शुक्रवार को पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के सक्रिय होने से पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में मौसम बदल सकता है। इस दौरान पहाड़ों में कहीं-कहीं हल्की वर्षा होने की संभावना है। इससे तापमान में बदलाव देखने को मिल सकता है। दिन में तेज धूप और रात में गिरते तापमान के बीच लोगों को मौसम के अनुसार दिनचर्या में बदलाव करने की सलाह दी जाती है।

- कॉपी लिंक
बिहार में धीरे-धीरे मौसम का मिजाज बदलने लगा है। मौसम वैज्ञानिकों के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक, आज भी राज्य के सभी जिलों में मौसम के सामान्य बने रहने की संभावना है। दिन में धूप खिली रहेगी, जबकि सुबह और शाम के समय हल्की ठंडक महसूस हो सकती है।
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, आज बिहार के किसी भी जिले में मौसम में बड़े बदलाव की संभावना नहीं है। प्रदेश के ज्यादातर हिस्सों में आसमान साफ रहने और दिन में तेज धूप निकलने का अनुमान है। वहीं, अधिकतम और न्यूनतम तापमान में 1 से 2 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट देखने को मिल सकती है।
मानसून की विदाई
दरअसल, मानसून की विदाई हो चुकी है। इसके बाद वातावरण में नमी है और तापमान में परिवर्तन हो रहा है। यही कारण है कि मौसम भी बदल रहा है। बादल नहीं होने की वजह से दिन में तेज धूप निकल रही है।
इस वजह से दिन में गर्मी का अहसास हो रहा। वहीं, अब दिन भी छोटा हो रहा है। इस वजह से न्यूनतम तापमान में गिरावट आने लगी है। मौसम के इस दौर में दिन और रात के तापमान के बीच अंतर बढ़ने लगता है।
पटना में भी मौसम में खास बदलाव की संभावना नहीं
राजधानी पटना में भी आज मौसम सामान्य रहने का अनुमान है। दिन में धूप निकलने से गर्मी महसूस होगी, जबकि सुबह और शाम के समय हल्की ठंडक रह सकती है। तापमान में मामूली गिरावट के कारण सुबह-शाम का मौसम पहले की तुलना में थोड़ा सुहावना हो सकता है। फिलहाल पटना में बारिश की कोई बड़ी संभावना नहीं है और मौसम शुष्क बना रह सकता है।
आने वाले दिनों में 20 अक्टूबर को बिहार में अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 23 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने का अनुमान है। इस दौरान दिन में धूप निकलने से गर्मी महसूस हो सकती है।
21 अक्टूबर को अधिकतम तापमान में खास बदलाव होने की संभावना नहीं है। हालांकि, न्यूनतम तापमान में करीब एक 1 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट आ सकती है। 22 और 23 अक्टूबर को भी मौसम सामान्य बने रहने का अनुमान है। तापमान में बड़े बदलाव के संकेत नहीं हैं।

The Department of Labor and Employment said it will issue labor advisories allowing employees to skip work and receive compensation during periods of extreme heat index levels amid the El Niño.
"Kapag 52 degrees pataas, extreme danger, ay pwede na huwag pumasok,” said Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino in an interview with Unang Hirit’s Unang Balita.
Additionally, DOLE will also ensure that employees in both the public and private sectors receive compensation for heat-related injuries sustained in the workplace.
"Ang patungkol sa ECC, Employees' Compensation Commission, kung saan ang ating mga manggagawa, pribado man o sa gobyerno, kasi under ng SSS at GSIS, ay magkakaroon ng reimbursement kung sakaling sila ay ma-ospital, magpunta sa clinic, at bibili ng gamot kung may heat-related injuries na work-related din,” said Tolentino, adding that these include heat stroke, heat cramps, and heat exhaustion.
The labor secretary said precautions should be taken during high heat index levels to protect workers, especially those working outdoors, such as construction workers.
“Nakasulat sa labor advisory na walang bawas sa sweldo… bawat kategorya po ay may mga kaukulang gawain si employer. Ganun din si employee na dapat sundin para sa kanilang kapakanan," he said in a statement.

Tolentino added that the agency will meet with representatives of delivery service companies to discuss guidelines aimed at protecting delivery riders, potentially allowing them to reject deliveries if the heat index reaches above 42°C. He said riders can take breaks at cooling hubs during extreme heat without penalties or risking their jobs due to delivery delays.
DOLE will also release an advisory allowing wearing breathable clothing in the workplace and implement flexible work arrangements to help employees cope with extreme heat.
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration earlier forecasted that the Philippines could face a “very strong” El Niño until December, and it is expected to persist through the first half of 2027.
The agency also warned that the country could still experience periods of heavy rain despite the generally drier conditions.
Meanwhile, the Climate Change Commission earlier said in an interview with 24 Oras that the heat index in urban areas, such as Metro Manila, could reach 50 degrees Celsius during the Super El Niño phenomenon.
Education secretary Sonny Angara said last week that due to the rising temperatures, public school students may come to class in tank tops or sando, as long as these are "dignified" enough for school.

Ixigo Q2FY27 results: Net profit hits all-time high of ₹63.42 crore
- Net profit hit an all-time high of ₹63.42 crore in Q2FY27 vs loss of ₹3.2 crore last year
- Revenue from operations grew 12.9% YoY to ₹320.96 crore
- Exceptional gain of ₹40.66 crore from Freshbus stake sale drove profitability
- GTV expanded 22% YoY to ₹5,304.47 crore with Hotels segment growing 159%
- Earnings call held on October 19, 2026, to discuss quarterly results
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Le Travenues Technology Limited (operating as ixigo) reported a consolidated net profit of ₹63.42 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, marking an all-time high compared to a loss of ₹3.2 crore in the corresponding period last year.
The company disclosed that it conducted an earnings call on October 19, 2026, regarding these financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, in compliance with SEBI regulations.
The turnaround was driven by an exceptional gain of ₹40.66 crore from the partial sale of its stake in Freshbus Private Limited. Excluding this non-recurring item and ESOP expenses, profit before tax stood at ₹33.53 crore, up 37% YoY. Revenue from operations grew to ₹320.96 crore, while Contribution Margin rose 14% YoY to ₹124.86 crore.
Segment Performance and Revenue Mix
The company operates across Flight, Train, Bus, and Hotel segments. The Train segment remained the largest contributor to revenue, followed closely by Flight and Bus segments. The Hotels segment saw significant revenue growth but continued to post operational losses.
Key Operational Metrics and GTV Growth
The investor presentation highlights robust top-line expansion driven by Gross Transaction Value (GTV). Quarterly GTV reached ₹5,304.47 crore, marking a 22% YoY increase. This growth was supported by strong performance in the Flight and Bus segments, which recorded GTV growth of 37% and 32% YoY respectively.
The newly disclosed Hotels segment emerged as a significant growth driver, with GTV growing 159% YoY (or 2.6x) to ₹111.34 crore. The segment achieved a gross take rate exceeding 12%, the highest among all lines of business. Management noted that the Hotels business crossed 4.7 lakh room nights in Q2FY27, growing 295% YoY, with over 86% of bookings coming from captive users. Hotel inventory stood at 70,000+ properties in India.
What the Numbers Show
A closer look at the financials reveals a divergence between operational profitability and reported bottom-line performance. While the headline net profit of ₹63.42 crore suggests robust earnings, ₹40.66 crore of this figure stems from the exceptional gain on the divestment of Freshbus shares.
Furthermore, other income contributed significantly to the quarter's results, standing at ₹22.08 crore, which is more than four times the ₹5.17 crore recorded in Q2FY26. This surge in other income, largely from interest on deposits and investments, alongside the exceptional item, indicates that the reported profit was heavily influenced by non-operational factors rather than core business expansion alone. Adjusted EBITDA declined 17% YoY to ₹23.58 crore, reflecting continued investment in technology and brand building despite the GTV growth.
The decline in Adjusted EBITDA despite Contribution Margin growth highlights a strategic shift in capital allocation. Management indicated that approximately ₹10 crore of the year-on-year cost increase relates specifically to building and scaling the Hotels business. Additionally, employee costs excluding ESOP rose by ₹16.9 crore, and technology costs increased by ₹4.5 crore, absorbing the ₹15.3 crore increase in total Contribution Margin. This suggests that core businesses (Trains, Flights, Buses) generated ₹126.1 crore in Contribution Margin, effectively funding the expansion into Hotels and AI initiatives like ixigo NEXT.
Balance Sheet and Cash Flow Highlights
The company's cash position strengthened considerably during the half-year period. Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹640.53 crore as of September 30, 2026, up from ₹344.49 crore in March 2026. This increase was supported by strong operating cash flows and proceeds from investing activities.
- Net cash flow from operating activities: ₹76.44 crore for H1FY27.
- Total assets: Increased to ₹2,726.21 crore from ₹2,541.31 crore in March 2026.
- Goodwill: Rose to ₹498.69 crore, reflecting recent acquisitions including Brevistay Hospitality.
Corporate Actions and ESOP Allotment
The Board also approved the allotment of 173,780 fully paid-up equity shares upon the exercise of stock options under various Employee Stock Option Schemes (ESOS). Consequently, the paid-up share capital increased marginally to ₹441,258,930. Additionally, PricewaterhouseCoopers Services LLP was re-appointed as Internal Auditors for the financial year ending March 31, 2027.

The IMD has issued a yellow alert for 17 districts, including Chennai, Tiruvallur, Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram, Cuddalore and Tiruchi, until October 23.
Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds reaching 40–50 kmph, with gusts of up to 60 kmph, are likely in parts of the state. Heavy rainfall is also expected at isolated places from October 22 to 24, suggesting that wet conditions may persist through the week.
Residents in the districts under alert have been advised to follow official weather updates and exercise caution during thunderstorms and intense rainfall.
Kerala and Lakshadweep weather forecast
Kerala and Mahe are likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall between October 21 and 24, with isolated heavy showers expected during this period. Lakshadweep is also likely to experience widespread rainfall, with isolated heavy showers forecast from October 21 to 23.
Isolated thunderstorms and lightning are possible over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep on October 21 and 22.
Karnataka weather tomorrow
South Interior Karnataka is likely to receive fairly widespread to widespread rainfall from October 21 to 24, with isolated heavy showers forecast during this period. North Interior Karnataka may see isolated to scattered rainfall.
Gusty winds reaching 30–40 kmph, with gusts of up to 50 kmph, are likely in parts of the state. Coastal Karnataka may receive isolated to scattered showers on October 21 and 22, with rainfall activity expected to increase on October 23 and 24.
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana weather forecast
Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema are likely to receive isolated to scattered rainfall on October 21, with isolated heavy showers forecast in these regions. Gusty winds reaching 30–40 kmph, with gusts of up to 50 kmph, may continue on October 21 and 22. Strong surface winds are also likely during this period.
Telangana may receive isolated to scattered showers on October 21, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds.
Weather forecast for northwest, central, eastern and northeastern India
The IMD has forecast no significant weather activity over northwest, central, eastern and northeastern India during the week. Most parts of the northeastern region are expected to remain largely dry from Sasthi (Bodhan) to Vijaya Dashami on October 21.
An IMD official said dry weather is very likely across all eight northeastern states — Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura — over the coming days. Maximum temperatures are likely to remain 2–4 degrees Celsius above normal over the next five days, while minimum temperatures are expected to remain near normal.
IMD's latest forecast
Rainfall is likely to continue across several parts of south India until October 24. Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal may receive isolated very heavy showers on October 21, followed by heavy rainfall at isolated places from October 22 to 24.
Kerala, Mahe and South Interior Karnataka are also likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall through October 24, while Lakshadweep may experience heavy showers between October 21 and 23. Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema may see isolated heavy rainfall on October 21.
With thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds expected across several areas, residents are advised to monitor IMD updates and follow local advisories, particularly in districts covered by weather alerts.

CHENNAI: Two weather systems are likely over the Bay of Bengal, with a low-pressure area expected to form over the southwest Bay of Bengal within 24 hours and another over the southeast and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal around October 23.
Meanwhile, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC), Chennai, has issued an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rain in several districts, including Chennai, and a yellow alert for heavy rain in other parts of Tamil Nadu on Tuesday (October 20).
An upper-air cyclonic circulation over the Gulf of Thailand and Myanmar is likely to move into the north Andaman Sea by Wednesday morning (October 21), the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Tuesday. It is expected to move west-northwestwards, with a low-pressure area likely to form over the southeast and adjoining east-central Bay of Bengal around October 23. The system is likely to move north-northwestwards and intensify further.
Separately, an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the southwest Bay of Bengal off the North Tamil Nadu coast now lies over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast, the RMC said. Under its influence, a low-pressure area is likely to form over the same region within the next 24 hours.
The RMC also said a trough extends from the circulation over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining Tamil Nadu coast to north coastal Andhra Pradesh.
Heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Ranipet, Kancheepuram, Kallakurichi, Tiruchirappalli, Ariyalur, Perambalur, Pudukkottai, Sivagangai, Tenkasi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts.
The northeast monsoon has gained momentum across Tamil Nadu, bringing widespread rainfall, particularly to coastal districts, the delta region and areas along the Western Ghats. Chennai witnessed continuous rainfall on Saturday (October 17) night.

Three years on from Storm Babet causing €200m worth of damage to homes and businesses in East Cork, local residents have little faith that long-awaited flood protection measures will ever be implemented.
Around 500 people recently attended a protest in Midleton overfurther delays to flood protection works that have been in the pipeline for a decade, even before the devastating floods of October 18, 2023.
Minister of State at the Office of Public Works, Kevin ‘Boxer’ Moran said earlier this month that Cork County Council will formally lodge a planning application for the Midleton Flood Relief Scheme “at the end of the year”.
In July he said that planning application would be lodged by September. Previous OPW minister, Kieran O’Donnell, had said it would be early 2026.
Caroline Leahy, whose home was severely damaged during the 2023 floods, told The Echo: “When the weather starts changing like this, we get quite anxious, because it takes only a couple of weeks of rain.
“Hearing about these El Nino storms is causing a bit of anxiety for people - not knowing what’s around the corner.”
Ms Leahy was one of the organisers of the recent protest.
“It was great to see the turnout, because you’re always a bit nervous that everyone has moved on and it’s just us, sitting here, afraid.”
She said that about 600 homes and 300 businesses are impacted, as well as surrounding villages, which will not even see their flood scheme start until the main Midleton scheme is finished, even though some have seen their homes flooded three times.
Ms Leahy said that three years ago: “We had about three foot of water come into the house in about 20 minutes.”
Residents were told that works could be done in her estate before the rest of the scheme as it wouldn’t have a knock-on effect downstream, and all the land needed was owned by the council already.
However, this project is now also delayed after the council found traces of asbestos in the area where they were planning to dig.
“Naively, we all thought the floods in 2023 were so severe, so drastic, affected so many people that they government would have to step in now and do something – that hasn’t happened,” said Ms Leahy.
“We know they have to go through the correct procedures and protocols and it has to be done right, but they’re talking about this scheme for more than 10 years, and there’s still not even a planning application in.
“At this point, we don’t have any trust in the system, that anything will ever be done to protect our homes.”
Ms Leahy will feature on a documentary this evening (Tuesday), exploring the growing impact of flooding across Ireland, while examining whether planning, housing and flood protection policies are keeping pace with a changing climate.
The documentary, ‘Ireland Under Water’, airs at 9pm on Virgin Media PLAY and Virgin Media One.
